1.

This petition is filed by the petitioners seeking following reliefs:-
"10.1.

The Hon'ble Court may be pleased to issue a writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to draw land acquisition proceedings under the provision of Act of 2013 to acquire the land of petitioners and to grant compensation in Manoj Jaiswani vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176818344/

sentences.text: 1 accordance with law.
10.2. To issue a writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondent authorities to produce the entire record pertaining to the present case for the kind perusal of the Hon'ble Court.
10.3. Any other relief/reliefs which may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case, may also be allowed.
10.4. Cost of the petition may kindly be awarded to the petitioner."

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioner No.1 became owner of the land bearing kh. no.254/2 admeasuring 0.121 hectares situated at village- Mohbhatta, Tahsil and Block- Bilha, District -Bilaspur.
The land was purchased vide registered sale deed dated 24.09.2013.

Petitioner No. 1 bequeathed some portion of the property in favour of petitioners No. 2 & 3 and accordingly, they have moved application for division of land according to the provision under the Chhattisgarh Land Revenue Code, 1959.
Respondent No.6 wrote a letter to respondent No.3 for acquisition of the land of 5.063 hectares situated at Village Mohbhatta for establishing Railway Siding.

Pursuant to the said letter, land acquisition proceedings was initiated according to provision of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short "Act of 2013").

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Land of the petitioners was also included in the preliminary notification issued for acquisition, however, at later point of time, land of the petitioners were segregated from the acquisition proceedings and other lands surrounding the land of petitioners were acquired.

He contended that after getting knowledge of acquisition of other surrounding land, petitioners submitted an application raising grievance that if land of the petitioner is not acquired, it will not be of any use for the petitioners as no approach road is available for approaching land of the petitioners.

Based on the application/letter written by the petitioners, Chief General Manager, District, Commerce and Industries Centre, Bilaspur had written letter to the Tahsildar for demarcation of the land and submitting his report.

Pursuant to letter of Chief General Manager, District, Commerce and Industries Centre, Tahsildar conducted demarcation and in the demarcation report, it is clearly mentioned that land of the petitioners is surrounded with the acquired land and on the both side, Railway Siding is to be established.
Existing approach roach is a private land of some other persons and if some construction is made by those private land owners, no approach road will be available for the petitioners to enter into their land.
However, even after submission of said demarcation report, no decision for acquisition of land of the petitioners has been taken.

As the proceedings of demarcation is initiated based on the application/letter submitted by the petitioners to respondent No.8 and decision is yet to be taken on the application submitted by the petitioners, respondents No.7 and 8 be directed to consider the grievance of the petitioners and take decision on the application with respect to acquisition of their land bearing kh. no.254/2 admeasuring 0.121 hectares situated at Village- Mohbhatta, Tahsil and Block- Bilha, District- Bilaspur.
3. Learned counsel for respondents No. 7 & 8 would submit that she may be granted a short time to file reply to writ petition.

She however submits that if the prayer of learned counsel for the Manoj Jaiswani vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176818344/
2 petitioners is limited to the extent of considering their claim and taking appropriate decision by respondent No.8, she is having no objection.

sentences.text: If the decision is yet to be taken on application submitted by the petitioners, it will be considered and appropriate orders will be passed in accordance with law.

4. Considering the grievance raised in this writ petition, submission of learned counsel for the petitioners as also document placed on record, in particular letter written by the Chief General Manager, District Commerce and Industries Centre to respondent No.5/Tahsildar on 10.01.2023 for demarcating the land of the petitioners in his presence and pursuant thereto, Tahsildar has already conducted demarcation and submitted report stating that land of the petitioners is surrounded by land already acquired by respondents No. 7 & 8, this writ petition at this stage is disposed of directing respondents No. 7 & 8 to take decision on the claim of petitioners on the basis of demarcation report of the demarcation conducted by revenue authority and pass reasoned order,
expeditiously, preferably within a period of 4 months from the date of receipt of order of this Court.
5. Petitioners will also be at liberty to submit fresh application for redressal of grievance in addition to pending application.
